title: Launch checklist — Hot-route capacity protection (Hosted API + Dedicated)
content:
Doc purpose
- This is the go/no-go + execution checklist for enabling hot-route capacity protection for Hosted API + Dedicated tiers.
- Includes: feature flags, config migration steps, canary enablement, monitoring gates, rollback criteria, and paging plan.
- Intended users: Release Eng, SRE on-call, Platform (gateway/routing/policy), Support escalation.

Change summary (what we are launching)
- Tier-aware gateway rate limits + quota evaluation (consistent 429 schema + headers).
- Priority classes + routing admission control using fleet capacity signals (enterprise traffic preserved; best-effort shed first).
- Overload event metrics + dashboards + alerts + incident-bot notifications.
- Feature-flagged rollout with region + account allowlists; reversible.

Scope of GA enablement
- Protected routes (MVP):
  - /v1/chat/completions (chat)
  - /v1/embeddings
  - /v1/rerank
- Tiers:
  - Enterprise: priority preserve + defined per-route budget
  - Best-effort/self-serve: earlier throttling and predictable 429s under pressure
- Regions: us-east -> eu-west -> (then follow-up enablement windows for other regions; not part of this checklist unless explicitly scheduled)

Key owners during rollout window
- Release driver: Talia Benson (Program Mgmt)
- Release engineer (flags/config): Benji Okafor
- SRE primary (monitoring gate + decision): Rafael Mendes
- Gateway (429 semantics): Amara Diallo
- Routing (admission control): Mina Haddad
- Control plane enforcement / policy engine: Ethan Park + Jordan Lee
- Observability dashboards/alerts: Sergio Costa
- Support escalation point: Dev Patel / Owen Phillips (FYI + customer-facing readiness)

Communication channels
- War room: #eng-releases (primary)
- Incident channel if needed: #incidents (create new thread; incident-bot auto-post should link dashboards)
- SRE coordination: #eng-sre
- Platform coordination: #eng-platform
- Support coordination: #support (FYI only unless customer impact)

Pre-launch checklist (T-3 days to T-0)
1) Code & config readiness
- [ ] Confirm merged + deployed to all target regions:
  - [ ] Gateway tier-aware limiter + 429 reason codes (ref: redwood/pr-27411, redwood/pr-27441)
  - [ ] Policy engine priority class evaluation (ref: redwood/pr-27418)
  - [ ] Routing admission control using capacity signals (ref: redwood/pr-27427)
  - [ ] Runtime queue depth + scheduler lag metrics (ref: redwood/pr-27435)
  - [ ] Feature flags + allowlist primitives (ref: redwood/pr-27452)
  - [ ] Debug endpoint gated (ref: redwood/pr-27477) — verify access control and audit logging enabled
- [ ] Config migration applied (route groups + tier defaults) without breaking existing configs (ref: redwood/pr-27512)
- [ ] Confirm no open P0/P1 regressions related to this launch (check ENG-4921 epic)

2) Feature flags (define “off”, “observe-only”, “enforce”)
- [ ] Identify flag names + current default values in prod:
  - hot_route_protection.enabled (global)
  - hot_route_protection.enforce_gateway_limits
  - hot_route_protection.enforce_priority_routing
  - hot_route_protection.admission_control.enabled
  - hot_route_protection.overload_metrics.enabled
  - hot_route_protection.incident_bot_notifications.enabled
- [ ] Confirm safe default = OFF for enforcement flags in all regions
- [ ] Confirm routing/policy will behave as no-op when flags are OFF (no perf penalty beyond minimal metric emission)
- [ ] Confirm allowlist keys and sources:
  - account_id allowlist (enterprise canary accounts)
  - route_group allowlist (chat/embeddings/rerank)
  - region allowlist

3) Observability readiness (must be complete before any enforcement)
- [ ] Dashboards deployed and accessible:
  - Hot route protection overview (tier breakdown)
  - Route-level latency (p50/p95/p99) + 5xx + 429 by reason
  - Shed/admission control rates over time
  - Capacity signals (GPU saturation, queue depth, scheduler lag)
  - Error budget burn for enterprise SLOs
- [ ] Alerts deployed (disabled or set to “monitor-only” until canary begins):
  - Enterprise route SLO burn-rate alerts (ref: slo-toolkit/pr-941)
  - Protection activation sustained (shed/admission > threshold for > N minutes)
  - 5xx spikes on protected routes
  - Unexpected increase in policy eval latency
- [ ] Incident-bot messages verified in staging (ref: incident-bot/pr-612)
- [ ] Metric cardinality check:
  - Confirm tier + route_group tagging only (no tenant_id, request_id, model_prompt_hash, etc.)
  - Spot-check recent metrics for label explosion (ref: redwood/pr-27488 hotfix context)

4) Support + customer readiness
- [ ] Confirm docs are up to date for 429 reason codes and retry guidance (ref: docs pr-2217)
- [ ] Support macro ready: “Understanding 429s: quota vs overload vs admission control”
- [ ] Escalation criteria agreed:
  - Enterprise canary accounts: page release driver + SRE if any sustained SLO risk or unexpected 429 surge
  - Best-effort: only escalate if global degradation (not expected shedding)

5) Rollout plan locked
- [ ] Region order and window confirmed:
  - Canary in us-east, then expand us-east, then eu-west
- [ ] Canary account list confirmed by Product + SRE (do not change during window unless rollback)
- [ ] Fallback/guardrail policy confirmed for protected routes (which routes may fallback vs strict admission only)
- [ ] Load test / game day learnings applied to initial thresholds

Rollout execution checklist (T-0)

Phase 0 — Pre-flight (15–30 minutes)
- [ ] Announce start in #eng-releases with participants + expected timeline
- [ ] Confirm on-calls are present / reachable:
  - SRE primary + backup
  - Platform gateway + routing
  - Observability
- [ ] Confirm no active incidents and baseline metrics are stable for last 30–60 min:
  - p95/p99 latency on protected routes
  - 5xx rate stable
  - GPU saturation within normal band
  - queue depth/scheduler lag stable
- [ ] Confirm recent deploys are settled (no rolling restarts in the last 15 minutes)

Phase 1 — Enable metrics + notifications (observe-only)
Goal: get visibility without changing traffic outcomes.
- [ ] Set hot_route_protection.overload_metrics.enabled = ON (all traffic, region scoped)
- [ ] Set hot_route_protection.incident_bot_notifications.enabled = ON (region scoped)
- [ ] Keep enforcement flags OFF
- Monitoring gate (hold 10–15 minutes):
  - [ ] Confirm dashboards populate and tags look correct (route_group/tier)
  - [ ] Confirm incident-bot posts ONLY on simulated trigger / staging validation (prod should be quiet)
  - [ ] Confirm policy eval latency doesn’t regress (watch gateway p95 overhead)

Phase 2 — Canary enforcement (us-east, allowlisted enterprise accounts)
Goal: enforce on a small, controlled slice.
- [ ] Set hot_route_protection.enabled = ON (us-east, allowlisted)
- [ ] Set hot_route_protection.enforce_gateway_limits = ON (us-east, allowlisted)
- [ ] Set hot_route_protection.enforce_priority_routing = ON (us-east, allowlisted)
- [ ] Set hot_route_protection.admission_control.enabled = ON (us-east, allowlisted)
- Monitoring gate (hold 30–60 minutes):
  - Enterprise SLO: no sustained burn (per SLO dashboard)
  - Latency: p95 not worse than baseline by > 10% for enterprise tier on protected routes
  - Errors: 5xx not elevated; if elevated, correlate with routing/admission decisions
  - 429s:
    - Enterprise: only expected quota-based; overload shedding should be rare in canary (investigate if present)
    - Best-effort: should be largely unaffected in this phase (since allowlist)
  - Capacity signals behave as expected: admission control triggers correlate with queue depth/scheduler lag (not flapping)

Phase 3 — Expand enforcement (us-east, all enterprise tier on protected routes)
Goal: protect enterprise broadly in the region.
- [ ] Expand allowlist to all enterprise tier OR switch evaluation to “tier == enterprise” for protected route groups (per config)
- [ ] Keep best-effort behavior unchanged unless explicitly included in this phase
- Monitoring gate (hold 60 minutes):
  - Enterprise: SLO stable, no burn rate > 2x sustained
  - Fleet health: total 5xx and tail latency not degraded
  - Protection activation:
    - If protection is triggering frequently, validate that enterprise is preserved and best-effort is shed first
    - Ensure alerts are not paging for expected best-effort shedding

Phase 4 — Enable best-effort shedding policy (us-east)
Goal: predictable throttling under overload for best-effort, preserve fleet.
- [ ] Set enforcement to include best-effort tiers for protected routes
- [ ] Confirm 429 semantics: reason codes/headers consistent across gateway + streaming
- Monitoring gate (hold 60–120 minutes depending on traffic):
  - Fleet health: p99 latency improvements or at least no regression under load
  - Shed rates: within expected band; no sustained “unexpected_shed” reason
  - Support readiness: sample 429 payloads from real requests and ensure docs match

Phase 5 — Roll to eu-west (repeat phases 0–4)
- [ ] Repeat with region-scoped flags: metrics -> canary -> enterprise -> best-effort
- [ ] Use region-specific thresholds (queue depth/scheduler lag) per Infra guidance

Go/No-Go gates (hard stops)
Stop rollout and rollback if any of the below occurs for > 10 minutes (unless SRE explicitly overrides with rationale):
- Enterprise route SLO burn-rate alert fires at severe level (per SLO toolkit) AND can be attributed to protection changes
- Sustained increase in 5xx on protected routes > +0.2% absolute over baseline (or customer-visible impact)
- Routing/policy overhead causes gateway latency regression p95 > +5ms (or > agreed budget) across broad traffic
- Metric cardinality explosion (ingestion lag, dropped series, or > 2x expected active time series)
- Incident-bot spams due to flapping triggers (indicates misconfigured thresholds or signal instability)

Rollback plan (fast path)
Order matters: restore behavior quickly; keep metrics if safe.
1) Immediate rollback (2–5 minutes)
- [ ] Disable enforcement flags in region:
  - hot_route_protection.admission_control.enabled = OFF
  - hot_route_protection.enforce_priority_routing = OFF
  - hot_route_protection.enforce_gateway_limits = OFF
  - hot_route_protection.enabled = OFF
- [ ] Keep overload_metrics.enabled = ON unless it’s the source of instability (cardinality) 
- [ ] Post status update in #eng-releases and (if applicable) #incidents with timeline + suspected cause

2) Secondary rollback (if needed)
- [ ] Revert config migration / route group mapping if it impacted non-protected routes
- [ ] Disable incident-bot notifications if noisy
- [ ] If performance regression suspected: disable policy eval cache/batch experiment flags (if enabled)

3) Escalate
- [ ] Page SRE lead (Rafael) if enterprise impact
- [ ] Page gateway owner (Amara) if 429 payload/header regressions
- [ ] Page routing owner (Mina) if admission control misbehaves
- [ ] Page observability (Sergio) if dashboards/alerts are wrong or cardinality issues appear

Verification checklist (post-enable)
Within 24 hours of GA enablement in a region:
- [ ] Confirm enterprise latency/availability improved during peak/bursty windows vs prior week (compare)
- [ ] Confirm best-effort 429 rates align with expectation; no unexplained 5xx
- [ ] Confirm top customer tickets: any new complaints? (Support to report in #support)
- [ ] Confirm alerts are actionable:
  - no paging storms for expected shedding
  - real issues page reliably
- [ ] Log final flag/config state in ENG-4921 epic + add note in release log

Operational notes / footguns
- Don’t change allowlist + thresholds in the same 15-minute window; makes causality impossible.
- If you see enterprise 429 “overload” reason codes during canary, treat as a bug until proven otherwise.
- If streaming clients report “inconsistent termination,” verify the streaming shed semantics fix is deployed in-region before expanding.
- Capacity signals can differ by region; queue depth is preferred over raw GPU saturation for admission triggers.

Pager / escalation quick list
- Release driver: Talia Benson
- Flags/config: Benji Okafor
- SRE: Rafael Mendes (primary), Aisha Bello (backup)
- Gateway: Amara Diallo
- Routing: Mina Haddad / Elena Popov
- Policy engine: Jordan Lee
- Observability: Sergio Costa / Allison Grant
- Support escalation: Owen Phillips

Runbook pointer
- If protection triggers unexpectedly or enterprise SLO is at risk, follow: Confluence “Runbook — Overload protection and admission control” (sections: ‘Interpret 429 reasons’, ‘Capacity signal sanity checks’, ‘Mitigation: tighten best-effort first’, ‘Rollback steps’).

Notes to self (release eng)
- Capture screenshots/links of pre vs post dashboards for the post-launch metrics review (ENG-4931).
- Add a short internal summary to #general once stable: what changed, what customers should expect (429 semantics), and where to find docs/dashboards.
